templates_considered: protect_health_data (recipe): used as the basis, all its templates and its custom access rule
audit_log_protected (RET-001): did not fit; needs audit_log table and record_audit_event function that do not exist; not built
approved_vendors_only (VND-001): did not fit; needs hosts or providers the customer has not given; not written
no_secrets_in_code (SEC-012): not in the health recipe; left out to keep scope to the ask
tables_classified / agreed_tag_vocabulary: not in the recipe; left out

rules.covers: health tables carry the phi tag
anything reaching phi tables requires login
endpoints do not fetch health fields
logs do not hold request, user or secret data
every access to health data records a log_phi_access call

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Audit log of changes to health data (RET-001)
Public appointments endpoint reaching PHI without login
Access reviews, staff training, BAAs, encryption at rest, backups, network
Health fields under names not listed

assumptions: phi is the health tag, as the recipe asks for CONF-012 and CONF-010
patients, appointments and clinical_notes are the only PHI tables in the workspace
reason, diagnosis, note, ssn, dob and insurance_member_id are the health fields
Customer approved the tagging and field-attribute changes in the plan, so I did not ask again
Endpoint auth stays unchanged: enabling login is outside the listed change types
confusions: Field attribute syntax for sensitive is not in the skill or catalogue examples; the inline {sensitive: true} form gave a syntax error; the block form { sensitive = true } worked on dry run
Table tag syntax (tags = [...] at table level) is not shown in the skill; I inferred it from endpoint tags
Recipe says CONF-012 uses the same tag as the access rule, but the template's own tag is confidential; the recipe's step to pick one tag is not explicit about overriding the template value
No guid was given for new objects; I left guid out and dry run accepted them
Skill's Ask first rules (for tags, auth, data) conflict with a build task where the customer pre-approved the whole change; I followed the brief
wished_for: An example of a table tag and a sensitive field attribute in XanoScript
A recipe note on how to pick one health tag and whether it replaces a template's tag param
Guidance on whether a recipe's template set should include RET-001 when no audit table exists
dry_run_problems_seen: Inline {sensitive: true} on a table field: Syntax error: unexpected 'sensitive:' (fixed with a block form)
why_confidence: The enforcement and rules are wired and the dry run is clean, but the public appointments endpoint and the whole-row patient response will still be flagged, and vendors, audit log, retention and the non-policy controls are not covered. This covers the health-data tagging, field marking and access logging, not HIPAA as a whole.
